_about: The mine (scripts/mine/mine_floor.gd, Game.mine_swing). The cave mouth on the `entrance_map` leads down to `floor_map`, a cave whose rocks, soft spots and way down are laid out fresh on every entry from a seed (MineFloor.make). The hammer breaks rocks (hits per rock kind, with the hammer's charge hits from data/tools.json), the hoe digs soft spots; each one hides a find picked when the floor is made, or the hole down. A floor band is the last one whose `from` depth is at or above the floor: counts are [fewest, most], finds are weights ("none" = nothing), per source (rock, big_rock, soft). Season factors multiply a find's weight. Swings cost stamina and fatigue like field work. Only the deepest floor reached is saved. Names and numbers are ours; see WORKLOG 2026-10-31 Mining.
_safe_radius: No rock or soft spot this close (in cells, either way) to where the ladder lets the farmer down.
_stairs: The hole down hides under one soft spot (that share of floors) or one rock, at least min_distance cells (x + y) from the ladder.
_seasons: Spring melt leaves the soft spots wet and full of clay; summer heat sweats amber out of old seams; fall is when agate turns up in the dry rubble; in winter frost opens the cracks where rock crystal grows.

landings.found: A rope lift hangs by the ladder. From now on it can take you down to floor %d from the mine entrance.
landings.ask: The cave mouth, and the rope lift beside it. How far down?

_landings: Every trip used to start again at floor 1, so the deep floors (15 and 20 for the ending's mine steps) took more food than a day can carry. Each floor in `floors` is a landing: a rope lift stands at `cell` beside the ladder (inside the ladder's safe square, so it never changes a layout; solid). Reaching a landing floor keeps it (saved in mine.landings, save version 6) and sets the story flag `flag`, which shows the lift's winch at the cave mouth. From then on walking into the cave mouth asks how far down: the ladder (floor 1) or the lift to any landing reached (the deepest three, a text box holds four choices). Starting at a landing never raises the deepest floor reached past what was walked, since only landings already reached are offered. Every fifth floor because a 150-stamina pack (the year bot's) goes about five floors in the mid-mine bands; 5, 10, 15 leave floor 20 one pack below the last landing. The texts are `found` (once, on reaching it), `ask`, `ladder` and `ride` (%d = the floor).
_light: Down the mine the picture is multiplied by the floor's light: depths are [floor, colour], blended in between (the last one holds below it), so each floor is a little darker than the one above. The farmer's lantern lights a circle `radius` cells across (`soft` = the share of it that fades out) in its own warm colour, the same on every floor, so it stands out more the deeper it is.
_winter: In winter the cold reaches down to floor `to`: those floors are frozen. Their light is multiplied by `light` (a cold blue), `frost` is the share of the open floor that lies white with frost (only a look), and `ice` [fewest, most] blocks of ice stand about. The hammer breaks ice in `hits` blows; it hides finds from `finds` (frost stone only grows in the ice). The hole down is never under the ice. Deeper floors are warm and stay as they are.
_items: Mine finds are rucksack items "mine:<id>": name, kind (stone / ore / gem), sell (G in the bin), look (icon shape and colours for PlaceholderArt). The Kurogane Smithy asks for ores in its tool upgrades (data/shops.json upgrades items); the shops buy stones, ores and gems by kind (their buys).
_prices: Deep finds were lowered twice once the rope lift let a trip start at floor 15 every day. First (WORKLOG 2026-11-03): kogane 90 -> 55, hoshigane 400 -> 220, jade 300 -> 170, amber 150 -> 100, rock crystal 120 -> 70 G and floors 13+ a blow more per rock: the year bot's year 1 winter mine 171766 -> 73160 G, still more than any whole season of the farm. Then (FEEDBACK item 4, WORKLOG 2026-11-04) about half again: shirogane 30, kogane 30, hoshigane 110, jade 85, amber 55, rock crystal 40, frost stone 50, and on floors 13+ a rock or soft spot hides nothing half the time. The aim: a winter of daily lift trips is a good side income next to the animals, under any farm season and far under a farm year. The ores keep their place in the smithy's upgrades (counts, not prices). The First Stone contest's rivals (data/festivals.json) were scaled by the same share both times.
